messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 spike detected for canary model v12 in us-west-2. Streaming p99 crossed SLO (target 800ms -> observed 3.2s). Paging on-call now. Alerts: streaming_timeouts, tail_latency, canary_traffic_shift.
oncall-bot: Links: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/2380012345 | traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/abc123

alex: I’m on it. grabbing dashboards, starting with live p99/p95 heatmap.

alex: Confirming: only canary cluster (canary-v12) showing the spike, prod stable for previous model. Traffic split was 10% canary -> 50k qps baseline.

devon: Logs show a growth in encoder timeouts and a handful of `KVCache miss` logs around the same time. P95 encoder increases from 60ms -> 450ms.

lina: Is this the new tokenizer change from v12? I remember a small tokenization change landed in the deploy yesterday.

sam: deploy-bot: Deploy v12 (model-hash: f3a9d) completed 00:24 UTC. Canary traffic ramp to 10% at 00:30.

maria: @alex can you confirm if batching config changed? Optimize suggested smaller batches for v12 earlier. Might be backpressure.

alex: Batching config unchanged on the route. But runtime metrics show queue depth increased on canary workers. I’m tailing worker logs now.

devon: snippet of relevant log: ```
[2026-03-15T00:35:12Z] worker-42 WARN encoder_process: tokenization slow: 320ms
[2026-03-15T00:35:13Z] worker-42 ERROR kvcache: miss serial=98432
[2026-03-15T00:35:14Z] worker-42 WARN streaming: stall detected, backpressure applied
```

lina: Could be quant mismatch causing slower attention kernels. v12 switched to 4-bit quant with new compiler flags.

sam: rolling back decision? We have to confirm customer impact first. Any user-facing errors?

cs-rep-jo: CS report: two customers reported longer response times in EU, but they were on global edge that routes to us-west. No error responses yet, just latency. One raised a ticket.

sre-lead: Paging ops: escalate to eng-platform if rollback needed. Prepare runbook: traffic-shift -> rampdown canary -> enable fallback to v11 -> increase worker pool if necessary.

alex: Quick mitigation: shifting canary traffic from 10% -> 0% (manual) to minimize impact. Executing now: `redwoodctl traffic shift --route streaming_api --from canary-v12 --to v11 --percent 10 --now`

eng-platform-bot: Traffic shift job started (job-id: ts-7721). Expect propagation 30s-90s.

devon: While shift runs, I’ll snapshot KV cache metrics and run a targeted test comparing v11 vs v12 tokenization path.

lina: If quant compile path is the culprit we should pin v11 quant profile as a fallback for v12 or keep v12 but force kernel selection.

alex: Traffic shift completed. Observed canary qps -> 0 in ~45s. p99 dropping back toward baseline. Monitoring.

oncall-bot: Update: streaming p99 now 780ms (within SLO). Incident severity downgraded to sev-2; continue triage and RCA.

sam: Good. We should still capture full traces and a reproducible minimal test. I'll open a deploy rollback ticket and hold v12 until root cause is identified.

devon: Repro test: local simulated load against v12 shows encoder p95 spike when tokenization buffer size > 1024 tokens. Might be a regression in tokenizer streaming state handling.

maria: Noted: tokenizer change pr-514 introduced a new buffer pooling behavior. Reverting that in a test branch now.

cs-rep-jo: Notifying impacted customers with a brief: "We observed elevated latency tied to a canary deployment; rollback applied; no data loss; engineering investigating; will follow up."

sre-lead: Action items: 1) eng-platform to block v12 from auto-ramping, 2) eng-ml to run quant/kernel compatibility tests, 3) devex to add telemetry for tokenizer buffer sizes, 4) cs to compile impacted customer list. Assigning owners.

alex: Taking owner for live mitigation doc + timeline. I’ll post the timeline in #postmortems after RCA.

maria: PR revert created: pr-602 (reverts tokenizer buffer pooling). Running CI and perf tests.

devon: We'll keep traces/logs linked here: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/abc123/details and perf artifacts at https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/2380012345.

oncall-bot: Incident closed for paging at 00:43 UTC. Triage continues asynchronously.

cs-rep-jo: I’ve emailed affected customers and scheduled an update at 03:00 UTC.

sam: Pushing a precautionary canary policy change: require 60m soak with traffic <1% before ramp. Filing RFC.

sre-lead: Good morning team — thanks for the quick response. Keep updates in this thread for RCA and follow-ups.

alex: logging final notes here: rollback executed, immediate p99 recovered, root cause suspected tokenizer buffer pooling regression interacting with 4-bit quant path causing encoder kernel slowdown under streaming loads. RCA in progress.

maria: will wait for perf CI; if green, we can attempt a guarded re-deploy with kernel pins.

devon: putting trace snapshots into the incident folder.

cs-rep-jo: closing customer comms loop once we have RCA.

sre-lead: end of thread for paging. Will convert to postmortem doc.
